subject: Renewal: Dedicated pool expansion + tokens-per-sec addendum
messages:
From: Jared Cole <jared.cole@atlas-robotics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>; Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lia Martin <lia.martin@atlas-robotics.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + capacity increase (need stronger throughput guarantee)

Vanessa / Rishi —

As we approach our July 1 renewal, procurement asked me to lock down the committed capacity numbers and SLOs for the Dedicated pool. We are planning to expand our reserved pool from 16 -> 24 A100-equivalent GPUs to support a new line of inference jobs (sensor fusion + multimodal routing). The key ask from our end is a clearer tokens-per-second guarantee for the reserved pool and an operational fallback in case of capacity shortages.

High-level asks:
- Baseline guarantee: sustained 150,000 tokens/sec across the reserved pool during business hours (PST)
- Burst capacity: ability to reach 450,000 tokens/sec for short windows (up to 5 minutes) 2x per day
- Credits or remediation language tied to unmet SLOs

Can Redwood provide suggested amendment language and a proposed schedule for the GPU top-up? We'd like to avoid a multi-week ops gap. Also include any impacts to price/term for the additional reserved GPUs.

Thanks — Jared
Jared Cole
Director, ML Infrastructure
Atlas Robotics
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Cole <jared.cole@atlas-robotics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>; Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>; Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity increase (need stronger throughput guarantee)

Thanks Jared — good to hear from you and congrats on the new workload. We'll put together an amendment that covers the GPU top-up schedule and explicit SLO wording.

Quick answers up front:
- We can reserve the additional 8 GPUs (bringing you to 24) with a target provisioning window of 7 business days after the amendment is countersigned.
- We typically express throughput guarantees as pool-level sustained tokens/sec over 1-minute rolling windows, with burst capacity defined as a short-window multiplier and a limited number of burst events per day.

I'm looping in Marissa on the SLO language and Rishi for pricing and the term adjustment. Stephanie from Legal will review the remediation/credits wording. We'll aim to have a draft amendment and a technical SLO appendix by Monday.

Best — Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>; Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>; Jared Cole <jared.cole@atlas-robotics.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft: SLO appendix (reserved pool tokens/sec + fallbacks)

Jared / Vanessa / team —

Attached are three items: (1) redwood-dedicated-amendment-v1.pdf (tracks the contract change), (2) capacity-upsize-schedule.xlsx (provisioning timeline), and (3) slo-language-draft.docx (technical appendix). Below is the key SLO language we propose — please treat this as the technical appendix to the amendment.

Proposed SLO (Reserved Pool Throughput)
- Scope: Applies to Atlas Robotics' Dedicated reserved pool (24 GPUs) for model-serving workloads routed to the dedicated pool.
- Measurement: Tokens/sec is measured as aggregate successful output tokens produced by the pool across all instances, sampled in 1-minute rolling windows.
- Baseline Guarantee: 150,000 tokens/sec sustained, available for at least 99.5% of 1-minute windows measured over each monthly billing period during Atlas business hours (08:00–20:00 PST).
- Burst Policy: Pool shall support burst up to 3x baseline (450,000 tokens/sec) for up to 5 consecutive minutes, up to two (2) such burst events per UTC day. Bursts are subject to available spare capacity; Redwood will notify Atlas if burst events exceed capacity constraints.
- Fallbacks & Graceful Degradation: When pool capacity is constrained, Redwood will: (1) preferentially route traffic to compatible model variants with smaller memory footprints (quantized profiles) where available; (2) enable prefix-KV caching for hot keys to preserve effective throughput; (3) proactively scale temporary burst capacity (subject to physical availability) and notify Atlas within 10 minutes of any capacity shortfall lasting >5 minutes.
- Remediation & Credits: If measured availability (as defined above) falls below the Baseline Guarantee in any monthly period, Atlas is eligible for service credits: 5% of that month's Dedicated charges per full 0.5% below the SLO, capped at 50% of that month's Dedicated charges. Credits are the sole financial remedy; other remedies may be discussed for repeated breaches in good faith.
- Reporting & Monitoring: Redwood will provide a dedicated dashboard for tokens/sec with 1-minute granularity, weekly SLA summaries, and an on-call escalation contact.

Operational notes:
- Provisioning: Additional GPUs will be billed pro rata from the activation date in the month of provisioning.
- Term: We propose a 12-month extension on the Dedicated contract tied to the GPU top-up; pricing reflects a tiered discount for committed capacity.

Please let me know whether the burst counts and credit schedule align with Atlas' risk tolerance. Happy to tune the numbers; the draft DOCX includes alternative credit bands if you prefer a steeper penalty curve.

— Marissa Cole
Head of Platform GTM
Redwood Inference
From: Jared Cole <jared.cole@atlas-robotics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>; Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lia Martin <lia.martin@atlas-robotics.com>; Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: SLO appendix (reserved pool tokens/sec + fallbacks)

Marissa / Vanessa —

This looks good and mostly aligns with internal expectations. A few quick asks:
1) Can we tighten the monthly availability target to 99.7% for Q1 of the renewal as a pilot, then reassess?
2) We need a clear definition of "compatible model variants" — can you add a short operational note that specifies quantization profiles (8-bit/4-bit) you will permit automatic fallback to, so our teams can test locally?
3) DocuSign flow — please send us the countersign-ready amendment with the SLO appendix and an invoice for the pro-rated GPU top-up. We want to get provisioning started the week after countersignature.

If Redwood can accept item (1) as a 90-day pilot with the same credit bands, we can accelerate approval on our side.

Thanks — Jared
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Cole <jared.cole@atlas-robotics.com>

Subject: Re: Draft: SLO appendix (reserved pool tokens/sec + fallbacks)

Jared — great, thanks for the quick review.

We can accept the 99.7% pilot for the first 90 days; Marissa will add the pilot clause and include the permitted quantization profiles (8-bit and 4-bit per-model whitelist) in the appendix. Stephanie will finalize the credit language to ensure it's consistent with enterprise procurement controls.

I'm attaching the countersign-ready amendment (redwood-dedicated-amendment-v1.pdf) and the provisioning schedule. I'll also open the DocuSign envelope and email the invoice once legal confirms final pricing with Rishi. Expect the DocuSign link within 24 hours.

Next steps:
- Marissa: add pilot clause & quantization whitelist to SLO appendix (by EOB tomorrow).
- Rishi: confirm final pricing and send invoice (by EOB tomorrow).
- Stephanie: quick review of credit language and countersign (as required).
- Jared / Lia: confirm signers for DocuSign.

Appreciate the partnership — look forward to getting you the extra GPUs quickly.

Best — Vanessa Ortiz

Redwood Inference
